title: Audit event lineage & actor/target graph schema for RBAC v2 admin flows
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Background: RBAC v2 introduces richer admin actions (role binds, policy changes, delegated invites) and tighter SSO/SAML identity links. Current audit events are inconsistent across services: actor identity shapes vary (email vs. SAML NameID), target references are sometimes opaque, and multi-step admin flows (canary rollouts, policy inheritance) lose lineage. Goal: define a single, backwards-compatible event schema and a compact delta/graph encoding that makes actor -> target -> resource lineage explicit, supports diff payloads for mutated objects, and carries identity confidence for SSO/SAML principals. Scope: server-side admin events (console + API admin endpoints) and backend-authoritative service bridges (authz service, hr-sync). Not in scope: end-user usage analytics or low-fidelity telemetry.
decision_notes: We evaluated two approaches for representing changes: 1) Full canonical snapshot (store before+after full object) and 2) Compact change-graph (store minimal set of ops). Decision: use a hybrid, canonical event envelope with optional compact change-graph payloads for high-cardinality objects. Rationale: snapshots are simple for critical security ops but expensive; compact graphs are efficient for frequent policy rewrites. The chosen canonical envelope fields are: event_id, timestamp, actor, actor_identity_sources (list), actor_confidence, action, target_refs (list), resource_types (list), change_encoding_version, change_graph (optional, compact), snapshot_before (optional, base64 gzipped JSON), snapshot_after (optional, base64 gzipped JSON), trace_id, parent_event_id (optional), service, region, retention_class. For change_graph we standardize on an array of ops with {op, path, value} where op in [add, remove, replace, move] and path uses dot/bracket JSONPath. Actor identity mapping rules: prefer stable SAML subject (persistent NameID) when available; fall back to email+principal_id. actor_confidence values: high | medium | low and we include supporting_attributes (list) with strings like "saml:eduPersonPrincipalName" or "idp_session_id". Change-graph is versioned; initial encoding = cgv1. Samples included below.
acceptance_criteria: All admin-type events emitted by authz-service and console follow canonical envelope with event_id, timestamp, actor, actor_confidence, action, target_refs, change_encoding_version.
Change-graph (cgv1) schema documented and parsers available in Go and Python libraries in repo (link in links).
A migration map for existing event producers is published and validated with staging ingestion (no data loss for P0 audit queries).
SAML subject mapping and actor_confidence logic implemented in authn bridge and tested against sample IdP payloads.
Retention_class tagging applied so long-term retention queries (security investigations) can be run without scanning ephemeral telemetry buckets.
